# The Cost of Intelligence, Episode 11: AI Got Cheaper. So Why Is Your Bill a Record?


### Token prices fell 21% in October and AI spend still hit a new high, Google’s top Gemini models double in price on 1 December, Wall Street weighs in on Jensen Huang’s exit, and an agent hires an intern.


[Strong Compute](https://substack.com/@strongcompute)


Nov 14, 2026


*Listen to this episode on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/1mdBiFi5OBq0YRiSsi0s9m) or watch it on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/VdMhp7VavtQ) .*


Welcome back to


**The Cost of Intelligence** , our comedy news show about the money behind AI. Each episode, Ben Sand reads the industry’s invoice and asks one question: are you getting more intelligence per dollar?


This week: Ramp’s card data says the average price of a million tokens fell 21% in October, and AI spend on its cards still hit a new peak. The unit price fell. The units did not. Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the cheapest model in the Gemini 4 family, while its bigger siblings double in price on 1 December. Happy holidays, from the pricing page. Nvidia fell as much as 14% the day after Jensen Huang’s exit and closed down about 4%, while AMD and Broadcom each rose about 6%. Nvidia sneezed. AMD and Broadcom sold tissues. And the Department of Token Efficiency honours Neon and Mubit, who sent an agent’s routine calls to a small tuned model and took about 70% off the GPT-5.5 bill. Here’s the written version, with every source linked.


---


## The tokens


AI reads and writes in tokens, chunks of words.


The world runs about


**467 trillion tokens a day** , on


[tokensperday.com](https://tokensperday.com/) ’s live model as of 13 November (a July estimate, grown to today). That’s about


**56,000 tokens for every person on Earth** , more words than most of us say in two days, and up about a trillion since Thursday’s show. Somebody left the agent on.


The site grows its count about


**7% a month** , on a Goldman Sachs forecast. That’s slow for a startup. Not on a base that big.


---


## The landlord’s rate card


*“Unlucky day to be a tenant. Every day is.”*


On the Ornn Compute Price Index, which tracks actual rentals, as of the 12 November settle:


-


**NVIDIA H100** settled at


**$3.39 an hour** , up about


**4%** since Thursday’s show and about


**8%** on the week (


[Ornn H100](https://data.ornn.com/api/public-index/gpu/H100%20SXM/index-history) ).


-


**B200** settled at


**$9.78 an hour** , flat since Thursday and up about


**3%** on the week (


[Ornn B200](https://data.ornn.com/api/public-index/gpu/B200/index-history) ).


Both chips got a raise this week. The old one got the bigger one. Same office, different HR.


Over the month it flips: the B200 is up about


**31%** , the H100 about


**13%** . Turns out the new hire negotiated better.


---


## Chips, power and the work


**Chips.** Epoch counts about


**34 million H100s’ worth** of AI chips, its last published count, from 21 October (


[Epoch AI](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-chip-sales) ). Call it one for every 250 people on Earth. Plenty of compute out there. You still need a reservation.


**Power.** AI data centres draw about


**30 gigawatts** . That’s our estimate, built on


[Epoch AI’s data-centre tracker](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-data-centers) : 19.6 gigawatts, including cooling, at sites covering about 44% of the world’s AI compute, scaled up and run at a typical load. The IEA-based count for last year is smaller: AI at about


**half a percent of the world’s electricity** , which is about


**a tenth of a percent** of all the energy we use (


[Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/how-much-energy-do-data-centers-and-artificial-intelligence-use) ). Roughly Ben’s own energy level by Friday.


**The work.** Our name for it this week is


**SI: Second-sourced Intelligence** . Intelligence with a backup supplier. Procurement’s favourite kind.


On our bet, SI does about


**11.6% of the hours we work** , about


**40 minutes a day** for every person with a job. Nobody’s sure which forty. Workers themselves say it saves them about


**2% of their hours** , per the St. Louis Fed’s latest survey, from July (


[FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/RPSGENAITSALL) ). That’s about seven minutes a day, by our maths. Forty minutes of work, seven minutes of credit. Welcome to the team, SI.


These numbers are a work in progress. Got better data? Step boldly into our DMs.


---


## The news: Google’s new Gemini


Google launched


**Gemini 4 Hydrogen** , the cheapest model in the Gemini 4 family (


[Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-hydrogen/) ). Fitting name: the lightest element, and the lightest bill in the family.


-


**Hydrogen:** $1.50 per million tokens in, $7.50 out.


-


**Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon:** launched at $2 in and $10 out. That’s an introductory price that runs through November. On


**1 December** it doubles, to


**$4 in and $20 out** (


[Gemini API pricing](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing) ).


Argon is a noble gas. Doubling the price is less noble.


Developer Simon Willison says he finds the pricing “really confusing” (


[Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/12/llm-gemini/) ). If Simon Willison is confused, procurement should lie down.


Today, Hydrogen only saves you 25% on Carbon and Argon. After 1 December, it looks like a bargain. Hydrogen, Carbon, Argon: the only thing that isn’t elementary is the pricing.


Back in 2024, Andreessen Horowitz named falling AI prices


**LLMflation** : for the same smarts, prices fall about tenfold a year (


[a16z](https://a16z.com/llmflation-llm-inference-cost/) ). At the frontier, come December, the price tag goes the other way.


*Per-dollar verdict: intelligence is cheaper when it’s less intelligent.*


---


## Ramp’s AI index


Ramp runs corporate cards, so every month it reads the AI line on a lot of bills. Ramp sees your AI bill before you do. Its October numbers (


[Ramp AI Index](https://ramp.com/data/ai-index-nov-2026) ):


-


The average price of a million tokens


**fell 21%** over the month.


-


AI spend on Ramp’s cards still


**rose about 1.7%** , to a


**new peak** .


William Stanley Jevons, what a paradox. You have a name for it too. It’s not printable.


And the spend is lopsided. The top 1% of firms spend about


**$10,200 a month on AI per employee** . The median firm spends about


**$16** , roughly 600 times less. Ten thousand a month per employee: better than an executive bathroom key.


Who gets paid? On Ramp’s cards,


**44.8%** of businesses pay Anthropic, up 1.1 points in a month, and


**40.6%** pay OpenAI, flat.


**SpaceXAI** trails both at


**6.3%** , but it’s the fastest climber, up 2.2 points. Somebody approve its expense report.


*Per-dollar verdict: the tokens went on sale. The bill didn’t.*


---


## Nvidia, the day after


Thursday’s show covered Jensen Huang stepping down as CEO (


[NVIDIA newsroom](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-ceo-transition) ). Then the market weighed in.


-


Nvidia shares fell as much as


**14%** early in the day and closed down about


**4.3%** , at $166.19 (


[Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/stock-market-today-dow-jones-s-and-p-500-nasdaq-11122026-12250329) ;


[Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/11/12/stock-market-today-nov-12-nvidia-shares-slide-on-reports-of-ceo-jensen-huang-s-resignation/) ).


-


That leaves them about


**30% below** their record close of $239.24 on 6 October (


[NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/nvidia-stock-huang-resigns-rcna608958) ).


-


**AMD** rose about


**5.9%** and


**Broadcom** about


**5.5%** , while the Nasdaq slipped less than half a percent (


[Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/11/12/stock-market-today-nov-12-nvidia-shares-slide-on-reports-of-ceo-jensen-huang-s-resignation/) ;


[Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/stock-market-today-dow-jones-s-and-p-500-nasdaq-11122026-12250329) ).


That looks like rotation: money left the leader for the challengers. Nvidia had a bad day. Its rivals had a casting call.


Interim CEO


**Colette Kress** stays on as CFO until a permanent successor is named. As one poster on X put it:


[Aden @anaden2023 Jensen's out. Colette Kress is now Nvidia's CEO AND CFO. She gets to approve her own budget. Finally someone at Nvidia running it like my household 😂⚖️ 2:31 PM · Nov 12, 2026 · 80 Views 1 Reply · 4 Likes](https://x.com/anaden2023/status/2120887269926342714)


Earnings come Tuesday,


**17 November** .


*Per-dollar verdict: second-sourced intelligence starts with second-sourced chips.*


---


## The tier list


How many dollars of API usage you get per dollar of subscription, on our 13 November run of Adam Holter’s method with


[Real API Pricing](https://github.com/Fei2411/real-api-pricing) . It ranks value, not usage. And they’re off!


[Adam Holter @AdamHoltererer Subsidization varies across users and usage patterns Some users get a lot more subsidization than others, but all of them get a ton This could be because the API rates for different types of tokens, such as cached input and output, might be different than the usage rates 10:51 PM · Nov 7, 2026 · 11.9K Views 8 Replies · 2 Reposts · 104 Likes](https://x.com/AdamHoltererer/status/2119201175904149984)


-


**Claude Max** is first out of the gates at about


**$77** of API value per plan dollar.


-


Then


**Claude Ultra** , about


**$66** , and


**Claude Pro** , about


**$64** (


[Claude pricing](https://claude.com/pricing) ).


-


Into the far turn: Claude Max on Haiku, Google AI Ultra on Flash, Claude Ultra on Haiku and Claude Pro on Haiku, around


**$46** .


-


Trailing the whole field:


**Google AI Pro on Gemini Argon** , at about


**$1.40** . Yes, the same Argon from our top story. Barely better than just paying for the API. That’s an F.


Good news, though: on 1 December, Argon’s API price doubles. Then this plan looks twice as good.


---


## Department of Token Efficiency


Somebody out there cut their AI bill. Let’s honour them the only way we know how. Safety goggles on, CFOs.


Today’s cost destroyers:


**Neon** , the database company, and


**Mubit** , a startup that tunes small models on an agent’s own work (


[Neon](https://neon.com/blog/mubit-neon-ai-gateway) ).


They ran an agent on GPT-5.5, then sent its routine calls to a small tuned model. The big model kept the hard ones. Which small model? Mubit doesn’t name it. It’s an open-weight model, trained on the agent’s own replies once a task has at least 25 good ones, and it has to pass an exam built from the agent’s own calls before it takes over a step. The agent hired an intern, trained on its own homework.


-


The GPT-5.5 bill went from


**$5.79** to


**$1.78** , about


**70% off** .


-


It finished about


**40% faster** (26 seconds down to 15.6).


-


Accuracy held up too: 60% before, 65% after.


Cheaper, faster, and no dumber. Apparently you can pick three.


**The fine print:** it’s a vendor demo. Twenty questions, run three times. The small model’s serving cost and Mubit’s own fee aren’t in the numbers. Some assembly required. Intern sold separately.


Worth a test, if your agent does the same chores every day.


Still: chainsaw approved.
